result_scope: binary64 result bits through the linkable support ABI (vf64_acos_rne for rnear_even, vf64_acos_round otherwise)

oracle.name: GNU MPFR
oracle.method: mpfr_acos at 53-bit destination precision with the binary64 exponent range installed and mpfr_subnormalize applied; the reference is the correctly rounded value, not an approximation

limitations: The support ABI is flag-free: exception flags and the per-call certificate are discarded, so neither is compared here; the soft path artifact for the same function gates both
The kernels call the symbols as unresolved externals statically linked against vf64-support.air with air-link, as a source-language backend does

Correct rounding is established per call by the certification test, not by a published hardest-to-round search over the whole domain; every case in this run certified, and an uncertified case would have failed the run rather than being delivered as proven

Ties-away-from-zero vectors are derived from MPFR_RNDN plus an exact midpoint test at 256 bits; acos of a binary64 is never exactly halfway between two binary64 values, so the nearest modes agree elsewhere
The corpus is seeded and stratified, not exhaustive; no claim is made about arguments outside the generated distribution beyond what the proof-obligation state establishes
acos is the only function in this artifact; each M9 function is published in its own artifact
